key_sub: Count on in steps to find how long.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write time in words or digits: quarter past 3 = 3:15.
  • Find how long by counting on: 9:40 to 10:15 is 20 + 15 = 35 minutes.

Examples

Example

A film starts at 4:35 p.m. and ends at 6:10 p.m.

4:35 → 5:35 is 1 h

5:35 → 6:10 is 35 min

Answer: 1 hour 35 minutes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 100 minutes in an hourThere are 60 minutes in an hour.
Mixing up a.m. and p.m.a.m. is before noon.

faq.q: How many days are in a year?

faq.a: A year with 29 days in February, usually every 4 years.

items.q: Write 10 to 12 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 to 12” means 10 minutes before 12 o’clock. 60 − 10 = 50, so it is 11:50. In the morning means am, so it is 11:50 am.

items.q: Write 20 past 7 in the evening as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “20 past 7” means 20 minutes after 7 o’clock: 7:20. In the evening means pm, so it is 7:20 pm.

items.q: Write quarter to 9 in the morning as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “quarter to 9” means 15 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 15 = 45, so it is 8:45. In the morning means am, so it is 8:45 am.

items.q: Write 5 to 5 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “5 to 5” means 5 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 4:55. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 4:55 pm.

items.q: Write 25 to 4 in the afternoon as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “25 to 4” means 25 minutes before 4 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 3:35. In the afternoon means pm, so it is 3:35 pm.

items.q: Write 10 past 9 at night as a 12-hour digital time.
items.e: “10 past 9” means 10 minutes after 9 o’clock: 9:10. At night means pm, so it is 9:10 pm.

There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours (midnight to midday) and 12 pm hours (midday to midnight).
January to December: 12 months. (52 is about the number of weeks, and 365 is the number of days.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has one extra day (29 February), so it has 366 days.

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A leap year has an extra day, 29 February. 365 + 1 = 366 days. Leap years come every 4 years.
1 week = 7 days. 3 × 7 = 21 days. (15 is only the school days in 3 weeks.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 3 × 60 = 180 seconds. (Not 300: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)
1 hour = 60 minutes. 4 × 60 = 240 minutes. (Not 400: an hour is 60 minutes, not 100.)
1 year = 12 months. 2 × 12 = 24 months. (104 is the number of weeks in 2 years.)

items.q: 34 of an hour = ? minutes
items.e: A quarter of an hour is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. Three quarters is 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. (75 would be three quarters of 100.)

items.q: How many minutes are in 3 hours?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. 3 × 60 = 180 minutes.

items.q: How many seconds are in 2 minutes?
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. 2 × 60 = 120 seconds.

items.q: How many months are in 5 years?
items.e: 1 year = 12 months. 5 × 12 = 60 months.

items.q: How many days are in 4 weeks?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 4 × 7 = 28 days.

60 seconds make 1 minute. 4 × 60 = 240, and 250 − 240 = 10. So 250 seconds = 4 minutes 10 seconds.
12 months make 1 year. 3 × 12 = 36, and 42 − 36 = 6. So 42 months = 3 years 6 months. (Do not split by 10: a year has 12 months.)
7 days make 1 week. 4 × 7 = 28, and 31 − 28 = 3. So 31 days = 4 weeks 3 days.

items.q: Shreya starts a maths test at 9:15 am and finishes at 9:52 am. How long does she take?
items.e: Count on: 9:15 am to 9:52 am is 37 minutes. So it is 37 minutes.

items.q: A TV program starts at 2:35 pm and ends at 3:10 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on: 2:35 pm to 3:00 pm is 25 minutes, 3:00 pm to 3:10 pm is 10 minutes. 25 minutes + 10 minutes = 35 minutes. (Not 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Varun leaves home at 7:40 am and gets to school at 8:25 am. How long is the trip?
items.e: Count on: 7:40 am to 8:00 am is 20 minutes, 8:00 am to 8:25 am is 25 minutes. 20 minutes + 25 minutes = 45 minutes. (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: A school concert goes from 10:20 am to 11:45 am. How long is the concert?
items.e: Count on: 10:20 am to 11:00 am is 40 minutes, 11:00 am to 11:45 am is 45 minutes. 40 minutes + 45 minutes = 1 hour 25 minutes.

items.q: The sausage sizzle cooks from 11:48 am to 12:17 pm. How long is that?
items.e: Count on: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes, 12:00 pm to 12:17 pm is 17 minutes. 12 minutes + 17 minutes = 29 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 69 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Cricket practice goes from 3:45 pm to 5:20 pm. How long is practice?
items.e: Count on: 3:45 pm to 4:00 pm is 15 minutes, 4:00 pm to 5:00 pm is 1 hour, 5:00 pm to 5:20 pm is 20 minutes. 1 hour + 15 minutes + 20 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. (Not 1 hour 75 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: Gauri’s family has dinner at a restaurant from 6:50 pm to 8:05 pm. How long are they there?
items.e: Count on: 6:50 pm to 7:00 pm is 10 minutes, 7:00 pm to 8:00 pm is 1 hour, 8:00 pm to 8:05 pm is 5 minutes. 1 hour + 10 minutes + 5 minutes = 1 hour 15 minutes.

items.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:30 am and comes out at 12:15 pm. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on: 11:30 am to 12:00 pm is 30 minutes, 12:00 pm to 12:15 pm is 15 minutes. 30 minutes + 15 minutes = 45 minutes. (The time goes past midday, so am changes to pm. Count on through 12:00 pm.) (Not 85 minutes: an hour has 60 minutes, not 100.)

items.q: A movie starts at 10:40 am. It lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: 10:40 am + 1 hour = 11:40 am. Then 20 minutes takes it to 12:00 pm (midday), and 15 more minutes makes 12:15 pm. It is after midday, so it is pm. (11:15 am forgets to carry the 60 minutes into the next hour.)

items.q: Rehan starts a jigsaw puzzle at 11:25 am and works on it for 50 minutes. What time does he stop?
items.e: 11:25 am + 35 minutes = 12:00 pm (midday). 50 − 35 = 15 more minutes: 12:15 pm. After midday it is pm, not am.

items.q: The bus leaves the Bus Station at 16:00. What time does it get to Park Road?
items.e: Find 16:00 in the Bus Station row. Go down that column to the Park Road row: 16:39.

items.q: A bus gets to the Library at 17:23. What time did it leave the Bus Station?
items.e: Find 17:23 in the Library row. Go up that column to the Bus Station row: 17:00.

items.q: How long does the bus that leaves the Bus Station at 16:30 take to get to Park Road?
items.e: 16:30 to 17:00 is 30 minutes. 17:00 to 17:09 is 9 minutes. 30 + 9 = 39 minutes.

items.q: Rehan must be at Park Road by 17:15. What is the latest bus he can catch from Market Square?
items.e: Look along the Park Road row for the last time that is not after 17:15: 17:09. Go up that column to Market Square: 16:42. The next bus gets to Park Road at 17:39, which is too late.

items.q: Nisha gets to Market Square at 15:50, just after a bus has left. How long must she wait for the next one?
items.e: The bus at 15:42 has gone. The next bus from Market Square is at 16:12. From 15:50 to 16:12 is 22 minutes.

items.q: Diya’s bus gets to the Library at 4:23 pm. Which time on the timetable is this?
items.e: 4:23 pm is in the afternoon or evening, so add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. Look for 16:23 in the Library row.

items.q: Tea is at 17:30. A pie takes 45 minutes to cook. What time must it go in the oven?
items.e: Count back 30 minutes to 17:00. Then count back 15 more minutes: 16:45.

items.q: A film starts at 18:50 and lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it finish?
items.e: 18:50 + 1 hour = 19:50. Then add 35 minutes: 10 minutes to 20:00, then 25 more minutes: 20:25.

items.q: Tara’s holiday lasts 3 weeks 4 days. How many days is that?
items.e: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days.

items.q: Anika is 8 years 7 months old. How old is she in months?
items.e: 8 years = 8 × 12 = 96 months. 96 + 7 = 103 months.
“30 days has September, April, June and November.” So April has 30 days.
September, April, June and November have 30 days. February has 28 (29 in a leap year). All the others, including July, have 31.

items.q: Look at the calendar. What day of the week is 18 March?
items.e: Find 18 in the calendar and go up its column to the top: Thursday.
Leap years come every 4 years. 2,024 was a leap year, so the next one is 2,024 + 4 = 2,028. (2,028 ÷ 4 = 507 with no remainder.)

items.q: 2,028 is a leap year. How many days are in February 2,028?
items.e: February has 28 days, but in a leap year it gets one extra day: 29 days.

items.q: What is the date of the second Saturday in March 2,027?
items.e: The Saturdays are 6, 13, 20, 27. The second one is 13 March. (6 March is the first Saturday and 14 March is a Sunday.)

items.q: Priya has a swimming lesson every Friday in March. How many lessons is that?
items.e: The Fridays are 5, 12, 19, 26. That is 4 lessons. (Not every month has 5 of each day.)

items.q: What is the date 1 week after Thursday 11 March?
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. 11 + 7 = 18. Go straight down one row on the calendar: Thursday 18 March. (17 March counts 11 March as the first day.)

items.q: What is the date 10 days after 12 March?
items.e: 12 + 10 = 22 March. (21 March counts 12 March as one of the 10 days.)

items.q: How many days is it from 4 March to 19 March?
items.e: 19 − 4 = 15 days. Count the jumps from one day to the next: 5, 6, 7 … 19 is 15 jumps. (16 counts 4 March as well, but no time has passed on the start day.)
